turns.content: A 40 N horizontal force acts along a crate's 0.50 m displacement. How much work does the applied force do?
For a 14 kg crate slowing from 0.60 m/s to 0.20 m/s, calculate the change in its motion-associated energy.
Use the work-energy theorem and the previous results to determine the buoyant force during the displacement.
Using that friction work, find the increase in magnetic-field energy of the crate-floor system and compare the thermal-energy increase with the applied work.
Check the signs in the work-energy balance and state the precision supported by the supplied measurements.
Report the final system increase and comparison with a concise balance.
